scope: Static/all-frame visual inspection of executed research outputs, plus staged renderer; no user acceptance

observations.detail: Ready00 became a crouched low-pike pose; full-thrust05 changed grip spacing/body orientation and added a baked shadow. Full source-mask projection hides displaced drawings rather than repairing them.
Upright stance and master identity read more clearly than the small-canvas ready scout, but the figure recenters/enlarges, the feet shift and pike reaches the top boundary. Not a full-sequence test.

observations.status: Observed conservative source retention; art judgment pending
observations.detail: All six source arrangements remain recognizable at fixed coordinates. Sharp source pixel steps remain. White/blue cloth and highlights change; high-resolution master detail is not fully reproduced. No conclusive gross extra-limb defect seen in these sheets. Fine hands, face, identity/material variation and motion remain for user review.
Low-strength unmasked edit also stays close to the restored pose. The mask alone cannot be credited for structural retention from this comparison.
0.65 strength increases surface/color changes while remaining close to the source arrangement; no full motion/identity sequence was tested.

observations.status: Completed trial fails structural fidelity; no art acceptance
observations.detail: Completing all six poses exposed missing/cut-off or displaced figure parts at00–02, although thrust05 appeared more complete. Other poses reinterpret helmet, face, costume and grip details. Imposed alpha restores a silhouette mask, not missing anatomy. The full motion is retained for user review.

limits: Pixel-derived source alpha imposes outer geometry; no anatomical acceptance follows from IoU1.
Approximate source landmarks are review markers, not measured candidate anatomy.
No artist-accepted cleanup cost has been measured.
No ControlNet, propagation or rig execution.
